intro: Administrative assistants keep offices running through scheduling, records and service, skills every organization needs. The closest of the 25 careers below is Office Clerks, General, with a 95% skill match, while Administrative Services Managers are an 83% match with a BLS May 2025 median of $114,130, or 140% more.
why_it_works: Your day is managing calendars, fixing problems for callers and making sure nothing falls through the cracks. O*NET rates time management and service orientation at 3.5 out of 5 for this job. Court clerk, HR assistant and office supervisor roles use the same organizing skills. Many matches pay about the same as the $47,540 median, so the real gains come from supervising or managing.
tips: Ask to lead a project, such as an office move or new software rollout, to build management experience.
Office supervisors earn $69,500, which is 46% more, and many are promoted from assistant roles.
Title Examiners, Abstractors, and Searchers earn $58,650, or 23% more, and value careful record work.

faq.q: What jobs can former administrative assistants do?
faq.a: The closest matches are general office clerks (95%), Correspondence Clerks (91%) and court, municipal and license clerks (88%), based on O*NET 31.0. Court and license clerks earn $48,700, which is 2% more than the $47,540 median for administrative assistants.

faq.q: Which careers for administrative assistants pay more?
faq.a: 13 of the 25 matches pay more. Administrative Services Managers earn $114,130 (140% more), office and administrative supervisors $69,500 (46% more) and title examiners $58,650 (23% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. The two management roles often expect a certificate or associate degree.

faq.q: Do administrative assistants need a degree to switch?
faq.a: Not for most paths. 18 of the 25 matches need no more education than assistants already have. In the closest match, 41% of workers have a high school diploma as their highest level, while HR assistant roles may need a certificate.

faq.q: What skills should administrative assistants build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are persuasion, instructing, negotiation and managing financial resources. Coordination already rates 3.12 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so leading people and handling budgets are the main steps toward supervisor and manager roles.
